thread:
zoe: heads-up: ran a quick smoke for helix-v3 q4 on staging. seeing systematic BLEU/chrF drops on our short-locale suite (ja / zh-Hant / ko / ar). repro + tiny examples below. anyone seen token boundary churn after quantizing?

zoe: repro:
```
./eval_local --model=helix-v3 --quant=q4 --locales=ja,zh-Hant,ko,ar \
  --dataset=short-locals-2026 --metrics=bleu,chrf --seed=123 --batch=64
```

zoe: quick snapshot (float -> q4):
```
locale    float_bleu  q4_bleu   float_chrf  q4_chrf
ja        34.7        29.4      51.0        45.2
zh-Hant   30.2        25.3      47.2        41.1
ko        31.1        27.0      48.6        43.0
ar        42.0        40.5      (N/A)       (N/A)
```

zoe: small failing examples: 
- ja src: "彼女は京都でガイドをしている。"
  ref: 彼女は京都でガイドをしている。
  q4_out: 彼女は 京都 でガイドをしている。  (extra spaces around kanji pair)

- zh-Hant src: "今天是測試，請確認。" (contains an IDEOGRAPHIC SPACE)
  q4_out: 今天 是 測 試， 請 確認。 (over-split, spacing)

- ar mixed src: "We met (اجتماع) yesterday."
  q4_out: "We met )اجتماع( yesterday."  (parentheses flipped around RTL run)

arjun: looks like resegmentation/empty-token insertion to me. ran tokenize-diff against the embedded tokenizer in both bundles.

arjun: tokenize-diff examples:
```
float tokenize("彼女は京都でガイドをしている。") -> ["彼女","は","京都","で","ガイド","を","して","いる","。"]
q4   tokenize("彼女は京都でガイドをしている。") -> ["彼女","は","京","","都","で","ガイド","...","。"]
```

arjun: note the empty token between the kanji split and the extra split inside the word. that will cause detok to insert spaces.

mei: same pattern for zh-Hant: float keeps compound token, q4 runtime yields many single-char tokens with empty entries interspersed.

mei: the ar paren mirroring probably comes from token-level reordering + our post-detok bidi normalization not being robust to zero-width tokens.

sato: checked build metadata: helix-v3:q4 image built 2026-03-15 with tokenizers@4.0.0-rc1; helix-v3:float image built 2026-03-16 with tokenizers@4.0.1. model bundle hash is identical in both images.

ci-bot: build note: model-bundle hash matches but runtime tokenizer versions differ. bundler currently does not enforce runtime tokenizer checksum at load time.

zoe: if runtime tokenizer differs from bundle-that-goes-in, we can get deterministic detok mismatches. sounds like a packaging/runtime mismatch rather than a model quant backend bug.

arjun: short-term mitigation: add a detok postfilter in eval harness that collapses empty tokens, removes stray ZWSP/ZWJ, and attempts to rejoin obvious split kanji/katakana pairs before scoring. ugly but quick.

mei: i'll prototype the detok filter and run it on the canary eval to see recovered delta.

sato: long-term: we should bake a tokenizer runtime checksum into the model bundle and have the model loader fail fast if runtime lib != checksum. also pin tokenizers in infra images used for canaries.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout updated: rollout_id=rl-2026-1900, hosts=3/3 updated, metadata: tokenizers: 4.0.0-rc1 -> 4.0.1 (note mismatch).

zoe: thanks. i'll open a GH issue with the failing samples, tokenize diffs, and the eval logs. ping here once the detok filter numbers are in. any other quick suggestions?

arjun: also add unit tests for katakana adjacency, ideographic-space combos, and bidi-adjacent punctuation in our scoring CI so future tokenizer patches fail early.

mei: agreed. adding tests to locale-smoke suite now. will post canary numbers in this thread. :+1:
